canonical_statement: The study compared unfractionated heparin dosing rates in critically ill patients with and without obesity, with emphasis on time to therapeutic aPTT.
Eligible patients were admitted to a surgical or medical ICU at a tertiary-care center and received a continuous UFH infusion for more than 24 hours between July and December 2007.

population.label: Adult surgical or medical ICU patients receiving continuous UFH >24 h

canonical_statement: Patients younger than 18 years, pregnant patients, and prisoners were excluded.
BMI groups were defined as non-obese 20.0-29.9 kg/m², obese 30.0-39.9 kg/m², and morbidly obese >40.0 kg/m².
Non-obese patients were started on UFH without a bolus at 16 units/kg/h using actual body weight.

exposures.details: Initial dose based on actual body weight; no bolus.

canonical_statement: Obese and morbidly obese patients were started on UFH without a bolus at 12 units/kg/h using actual body weight.

exposures.details: Initial dose based on actual body weight; no bolus.

canonical_statement: The institutional nomogram targeted aPTT 57-84 seconds for the standard range or 57-70 seconds for the cardiac/low range, with dose changes and holds specified by Table 1.
The primary dosing endpoint included UFH dose at the first therapeutic aPTT, expressed as units/h, units/kg ideal body weight/h, and units/kg actual body weight/h.

concept.text: UFH dose at first therapeutic aPTT

canonical_statement: Time to the first therapeutic aPTT was a primary endpoint.
Steady state was defined as three consecutive aPTT values in the applicable therapeutic range.

outcome.definition: Three consecutive aPTTs in therapeutic range: 57-84 sec for standard range or 57-70 sec for low range.

canonical_statement: Major bleeding was defined as a documented cerebral, gastrointestinal, or retroperitoneal bleed.

outcome.definition: Documented cerebral, gastrointestinal, or retroperitoneal bleed.

canonical_statement: Minor bleeding was defined as ecchymosis, epistaxis, hematoma, hematuria, hemoptysis, petechiae, or oozing.

outcome.definition: Ecchymosis, epistaxis, hematoma, hematuria, hemoptysis, petechiae, or oozing.

canonical_statement: Continuous data were analyzed with ANOVA for parametric data and Kruskal-Wallis for non-parametric data; categorical data used Fisher exact testing, with P<0.05 considered significant.
The analysis included 62 critically ill patients: 21 non-obese, 21 obese, and 20 morbidly obese.
Non-obese patients had mean body weight 67 kg (Table 2).
Non-obese patients had mean BMI 24.2 kg/m² (Table 2).
Obese patients had mean body weight 93.5 kg (Table 2).
Obese patients had mean BMI 34.1 kg/m² (Table 2).
Morbidly obese patients had mean body weight 160.3 kg (Table 2).

canonical_statement: Morbidly obese patients had mean BMI 55.3 kg/m² (Table 2).

Using actual body weight with a reduced initial UFH dose in obese and morbidly obese critically ill patients was associated with similar time to first therapeutic aPTT and steady state across BMI groups.
The authors concluded that the initial weight-based UFH rate should be reduced in obese and morbidly obese critically ill patients.
The retrospective design and small sample size may have left the study underpowered to detect between-group differences.
Only about half of patients achieved steady state, reducing the evaluable population and statistical power for steady-state endpoints.
Potential contributors to UFH dosing variability, including age, race, gender, renal function, tobacco use, indication, diabetes, and thyroid disease, were not evaluated.
The single-center study used a specific UFH dosing protocol, limiting generalizability to other populations and protocols.
The article reported no source of support.
